consumer_seed: The Project Gigabit Evaluation Plan page was published on 15 August 2025.
Building Digital UK is described as an executive agency within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology.
BDUK commissioned Ipsos UK and partners to undertake the Project Gigabit evaluation.
The evaluation includes the Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy and the Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme interventions.
The report sets out a recommended evaluation approach for Project Gigabit and for the GIS and GBVS interventions individually.
Project Gigabit is described as targeting hard-to-reach communities with fast, reliable gigabit-capable broadband.
The programme targets homes and businesses not included in broadband suppliers' commercial plans.
GIS awards subsidised contracts to network providers where commercial delivery would otherwise not be viable.
The evaluation-plan page describes gigabit-capable networks as offering download speeds of at least 1,000 Mbps.
The GBVS mechanism is described as providing vouchers worth up to £4,500 to homes and businesses for installation costs.
The Map Your Mobile milestone article was published on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used Map Your Mobile.
Map Your Mobile is described as a free mobile coverage checker.
Users can enter a postcode to view networks available in that area.
The checker provides a score showing which company performs best in the user's postal district.
The checker is intended to help users compare networks before signing up or switching.
The checker uses crowdsourced Opensignal data based on people's real experiences.
The checker also uses predictive information from UK mobile networks.
Ofcom says the checker is regularly updated with fresh data.
The checker can indicate whether coverage is likely to work inside the home.
The Q4 2025 telecoms complaints article was published on 11 May 2026.
The figures cover October to December 2025.
Overall complaints increased on the previous quarter for the first time since 2023.
Complaints about broadband and landline services decreased in Q4 2025.
Pay-TV complaints stayed at the same level in Q4 2025.
TalkTalk and Vodafone were the most complained-about broadband providers in the Q4 2025 release.
Plusnet and Virgin Media were the least complained-about broadband providers in the Q4 2025 release.
O2 generated the most mobile complaints in the Q4 2025 release.
EE generated the most pay-TV complaints in the Q4 2025 release.
The Comparing Customer Service page was published on 18 May 2023.
The Comparing Customer Service page was last updated on 25 May 2026.
The current publication is Ofcom's eighth report comparing residential telecoms customer-service levels.
The report covers residential customer-service levels and experiences in 2024 and compares them with 2022 and/or 2023.
Ofcom reported that overall satisfaction among mobile, broadband and landline customers remained high.
Some EE broadband and landline faults data for 2024 and associated industry averages were identified as subject to restatement.
The ADR schemes' performance page was published on 26 January 2024.
The ADR schemes' performance page was last updated on 23 July 2026.
Ofcom publishes quarterly KPI results for CISAS and Communications Ombudsman.
Ofcom updated the ADR-scheme KPIs from Q4 2025.
Ofcom is the competent authority for the UK communications and postal sectors under the cited ADR regulations.
Ofcom must assess every two years whether ADR schemes continue to meet the regulatory requirements.
expansion_rule: For each contract in the union of the October 2025 and July 2026 tables emit eleven records. Contracts present in both months receive: presence classification, contracted delta, built delta, contracted percentage change, built percentage change or zero-base guard, average monthly contracted delta, average monthly built delta, October gap, July gap, gap change, and built increase as a percentage of the October gap or zero-gap guard. A contract present in only one month receives month-specific supplier/count/gap facts and explicit missing-month guards without imputation. Append 42 official evaluation, checker, complaints, service-quality and ADR records. Every fifth expanded record is REVALIDATION; all others are UPGRADE.
